newsitem.title: UK: Strong North Sea leads gain for Dirty tanker rates.
newsitem.headline: Strong North Sea leads gain for Dirty tanker rates.

text.p: Dirty oil tanker chartering rates were mixed on Friday. Rates for Aframax and Suezmax tonnage were generally firmer in good demand while slower demand left VLCC and ULCC rates around steady, brokers said.
"The VLCC market has drifted and could go either way," brokers Galbraith's said in their weekly report.

However, the trend for smaller Suezmax and more particularly Aframax tonnage was more clearly defined with strong demand from European refiners for boosting rates for Inter UK/Cont voyages for 80,000 tonne vessels by around 35 points to W140, equivalent to a $1 per tonne rise since last Friday.
Middle East Gulf markets were mostly stable with an increase in vessel availability balanced by increased fixings to the West, while demand for voyages to Singapore and Japan stayed thin.
Transatlantic trade from West Africa slowed on Friday but a busy week saw rates for VLCC and Suezmax trips to the U.S. Gulf holding firm around W70 and W107.5 respectively.
Med/Black Sea activity was also thinner today. Cross-Med trips for Aframax tonnage talked slightly weaker around W100. ULCCs moved cross-Med out of Sidi Kreir at around W172.5-W180.
